item.title: From Tasmania’s 100% Green Power to Victoria’s Delays: Mapping Australia’s Energy Divide
item.description: Australia is making strides in the renewable transition, with the country’s renewables recently hitting a record 76.4 percent share of electricity demand on the National Electricity Market. From it's 40% rooftop solar penetration to the numerous 'big batteries', both existing and planned dotting the continent, it has provided a roadmap for many others to follow. As per data and analytics firm GlobalData, renewables are expected to account for 73.3 percent of the country’s total power generation

item.title: C&I Developers Expected to Add 60-80 GW of Renewable Capacity by 2030: MNRE Secretary
item.description: India’s commercial and industrial (C&I) developers are set to play a pivotal role in the country’s renewable energy trajectory, contributing an estimated 60-80 GW of clean energy capacity by 2030, according to Santosh Kumar Sarangi, Secretary of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE). item.title: NREL Renamed As National Laboratory Of the Rockies in the US
item.description: Continuing with its inexorable drift away from renewable goals and commitments, the US Department of Energy (DOE) has renamed the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) the National Laboratory of the Rockies. The change follows significant staff cuts at the NREL a few months back, and will seek to douse any further role for the organisation in being among the frontrunners of research and data on renewable energy, particularly solar and wind. item.title: AMPIN Energy Transition Raises USD 50 Mn from Dutch Bank for Greenfield RE Projects
item.description: AMPIN Energy Transition Private Limited secured USD 50 million in investment from FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank, to develop greenfield renewable energy projects. The company explained in a press release that it will use this long-term investment to support its continued expansion of the renewable energy portfolio across India. item.title: After EPC Business, AB Energia Plans to Expand Its Solar Mounting Structure Manufacturing
item.description: Indian renewable EPC company AB Energia, which recently entered the solar mounting-structure business, is now planning to expand its manufacturing capabilities. According to the company’s top management, its current annual production capacity of solar structures is around 400 MW, and it aims to scale this up to 700 MW soon. item.title: Terra Clean Invites Bids for Land Aggregation in Gujarat for 300 MW Solar Project
item.description: Terra Clean, a wholly owned subsidiary of Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), has issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) seeking bids for land aggregation to facilitate a large-scale solar power project in Gujarat. The proposal focuses on securing land for a 300 MW intrastate transmission system (InSTS)-connected solar project, with an additional greenshoe option of up to 300 MW.
